title: Data Structures & Algorithm Basics
intro: Data structures and algorithm questions for Python freshers test whether you can think about efficiency, not just correctness. This page covers Big-O notation at the concept level (O(1), O(n), O(n²) — with Python list examples so the theory connects to code you already write), arrays and Python lists (how list operations like append and insert differ in complexity), the linked list concept (node + pointer, why it exists even though Python has list), stacks and queues (LIFO vs FIFO, how to implement both using Python list and collections.deque), basic recursion (how a recursive function calls itself, base case, the call stack — with factorial and fibonacci as examples), and hash tables (the dict under the hood, why O(1) lookup is not magic). These are concept-level questions at fresher interviews — you won't be asked to implement a red-black tree, but you will be asked 'why is dict lookup faster than list search?'
